threat: traffic analysis of relay delivery
residual_risk: global passive observer timing correlation remains without anonymity transports

threat: substituted ContactDescriptor/keys
residual_risk: trust-on-first-use until manual/continuity verification

threat: correlating stable queue identifiers
residual_risk: per-relay timing/volume

threat: split identity views/equivocation
residual_risk: no global transparency root in v1

threat: blob deletion or corruption
residual_risk: availability loss without redundancy

threat: media decryption/injection
residual_risk: call metadata to media provider

threat: cross-provider correlation
residual_risk: collusion defeats provider separation

threat: introduction floods
residual_risk: Sybil identities are cheap; reach is bounded

threat: abuse of legitimate grants
residual_risk: legitimate authority can be misused; fork/leave remains

threat: seizing account via quarantine/promotion
residual_risk: single-controller accounts are taken over by one compromise

threat: resurrecting revoked devices/policies
residual_risk: isolated device without gossip may be partitioned

threat: recovery becoming a master key
residual_risk: guardian collusion at configured threshold

threat: CryptoProfile stripping downgrade
residual_risk: first contact with no established floor

threat: same-epoch MLS fork or policy/MLS divergence
residual_risk: coordinator liveness under partition

threat: one-time key split-brain
residual_risk: last-resort key reuse under depletion

threat: parser/decoder exploitation via media, packs or rich text
residual_risk: platform decoder zero-days

threat: link-preview SSRF/rebinding
residual_risk: preview fetch reveals recipient activity unless proxied

threat: malicious release
residual_risk: targeted store-signed builds remain hard to detect

threat: malicious JavaScript from the ClientHost origin
residual_risk: browser platform cannot prevent a compromised origin; native is higher assurance

adversary: single cloud vendor (policy, filter, outage, coercion)
threat: vendor-wide disabling of OM Homes (monoculture)
residual_risk: relationships whose every route is on one vendor lose routes until re-homing

threat: deploying malicious ClientHost code for one user
residual_risk: targeted substitution detectable only by independent observation

threat: silently linking an extra device
residual_risk: notice depends on victim seeing another device

threat: reading an unlocked device
residual_risk: unlocked device reveals retained data; no deniability promised

adversary: OS/cloud backup service or its compromiser
threat: plaintext/key copies in device backups
residual_risk: platforms without exclusion controls

threat: app-switcher snapshots/screenshots
residual_risk: PWA cannot suppress snapshots

threat: IME learning or cloud spellcheck upload
residual_risk: OS-level tools may ignore page hints

threat: reading the decrypted DOM
residual_risk: cannot be prevented by a web page; disclosed

adversary: other users of a shared device
threat: cross-user access on one OS account
residual_risk: shared OS account is not a private place

threat: harvest-now-decrypt-later against classical v1 MLS
residual_risk: v1 group traffic recorded before PQ migration stays exposed

threat: LLM tool misuse or escalation
residual_risk: granted capabilities can still be misused within scope

threat: ambient authority or exfiltration
residual_risk: granted plaintext-read plus user-approved egress

threat: spoofed foreign identity, loops, reflection
residual_risk: bridge sees plaintext by design

threat: authority cloning or fabricated history via import
residual_risk: imported history is only as honest as its source

threat: project governance becoming protocol authority
residual_risk: founder-only S0 custody until co-stewards exist

threat: exploitation of known vulnerabilities without a kill switch
residual_risk: unupdated peers remain vulnerable; peers see 'needs update'

threat: denial of service by quota exhaustion
residual_risk: free tiers fail closed; availability loss

threat: confusable names/copied avatars
residual_risk: users may ignore warnings

threat: evidence that only confirms its author's assumptions
residual_risk: independent reviewers may share blind spots

adversary: impersonator of an abandoned account / stale route
threat: messages sent to a dead or hijacked abandoned identity
residual_risk: unretired lost accounts look merely offline

threat: illegal content hosted on public Publications/catalogs/blob hosts
residual_risk: private E2EE content is not scanned by design

adversary: attacker holding a recovery custodian (phished platform account, found recovery key, colluding guardians)
threat: takeover through default recovery
residual_risk: a user with no remaining device cannot veto within the delay; the attacker wins that race. Disclosed in the ContinuityAssessment.

adversary: attacker who compromises a T1 host's hosting account
threat: malicious ClientHost JavaScript served to every member of a community Home
residual_risk: members who explicitly opt into the host's ClientHost inherit the host's account security

threat: repeated recovery requests to exhaust the user's vigilance (veto fatigue)
residual_risk: notices repeat until the user rotates custody; rotation is guided after the first veto

adversary: a compromised or mistaken design agent, or a tampered zip
threat: silent regression or malicious change introduced through an imported design drop
residual_risk: the validator catches contract violations, not every semantic regression; the operator must review each drop's merge diff

threat: synced-passkey custody reveals that a platform account uses an OM distribution
residual_risk: the rpId reveals OM use to the credential vault; Maximum Privacy avoids platform custody

threat: custodian alone permanently revokes controllers or retires the account with no delay or veto
residual_risk: a user with no live device and a compromised custodian loses the race (T-041)

adversary: stolen messaging device or colluding guardians
threat: a successor pointer redirects every relationship to an attacker account while the owner keeps working devices
residual_risk: a constitutional majority (or recovery vote after delay without veto) can still move the account

threat: substitutes the intro identity or request key, or learns the sender's identity from the first-contact request
residual_risk: trust-on-first-use without key transparency until safety-number verification; IntroGate sees timing, size and network address

threat: publishes a newer RelaySet or BlobLocationRecord pointing at attacker queues, blackholing delivery and collecting metadata
residual_risk: a peer that has not yet seen the quarantine may accept one set until it syncs control state

adversary: anyone who learns a device id; KeyMaterialProvider
asset: one-time forward secrecy and account unlinkability
threat: drains one-time prekey pools and groups devices per account via acs_state_hash
residual_risk: acs_generation/acs_state_hash still link an account's devices across providers until A-031

threat: forged referrals consume the R-195 reserved queue
residual_risk: a contact who leaks tokens can admit strangers up to the tokens issued

adversary: network attacker or hostile peer arguing compatibility
threat: forces a downgrade through an undefined floor exception or by comparing profile ids
residual_risk: a forged SecurityAdvisory is bounded by advisory signature rules (ADR-0104) and never lowers the generation

adversary: device seizer, coercer or any member holding decrypted group messages
threat: MLS leaf signatures chaining to AccountID let a third party verify group transcripts of other members' messages
residual_risk: inherent to RFC 9420 authentication; OM documents it honestly; deniable groups would need a research ADR (A-036)

adversary: offline, lost or malicious CommitCoordinator device
asset: liveness of security reductions (revocation, removal, leave)
threat: coordinator delays or censors removal of a compromised device, a member, or itself
residual_risk: a revoked device keeps receiving group secrets for up to sequencing_timeout plus propagation delay

adversary: spammer or stranger who is (or befriends) a group member
threat: unsolicited group add or KeyPackage harvest reveals the invitee's AccountID and devices to every member; a leaked invite link outlives its issuer
residual_risk: an accepted invitee's identity is visible to all members by design

adversary: Room member, full-room service or bridge not joined to a call, colluding with an untrusted SFU
threat: a non-joined Room endpoint derives the exporter-based call key and silently listens to SFU-forwarded streams
residual_risk: open until A-035 selects an isolation mechanism; key-capable services and bridges are shown in the call UI

adversary: holder of a compromised Publication signing key; withholding mirror
asset: integrity of a public Publication feed
threat: backdated posts signed after revocation verify as pre-revocation; mirrors withhold revocations and tombstones
residual_risk: a subscriber that never sees the revocation keeps accepting the key's posts; withholding delays but cannot roll back a seen head

adversary: group member who creates a HistoryBundle
asset: authenticity of pre-join history shown to newcomers
threat: bundle author invents or alters other members' past messages
residual_risk: newcomers must trust the bundle author for content; the UI attributes it to that author

asset: group membership and Room identity privacy
threat: raw MLS messages expose group_id and epoch, letting relays link copies across recipients and providers and possibly learn the ConversationID
residual_risk: timing and size correlation remain; a group_broadcast provider sees recipient-set linkage by declaration

adversary: malicious or compromised local plugin, or a local LLM running as one
threat: extension code sends events that recipients see as authored by the account with no human review
residual_risk: a user who confirms content they did not read closely still authors it

adversary: one Room member's personal plugin, service or automation
asset: confidentiality of other members' Room plaintext
threat: continuous export of Room plaintext on one member's local grant, invisible to other members
residual_risk: a member can still copy or screenshot manually; a modified client ignores taint (absolute rule 11)

adversary: holder of a briefly accessed or stolen messaging device
threat: minting RepresentationGrants that let a service post as 'Alice · via X' or receive counterparties' messages without their knowledge
residual_risk: a stolen control device can issue grants until quarantined; other devices see the notice

adversary: attacker holding a compromised service endpoint key
asset: confidentiality of Rooms where the service is installed
threat: revoked endpoint keeps receiving Room plaintext because no member learns of or commits its removal
residual_risk: exposure until the first member receives the head plus sequencing_timeout (ADR-0122 rule 8)

adversary: operator of a shared ClientHost, or an attacker who compromises its hosting account
asset: endpoint integrity of every user it serves
threat: malicious JavaScript served to all T0/T1 PWA users of a shared origin
residual_risk: a fully compromised origin can serve targeted code the digest check misses (CLIENTHOST §3); native clients remain the higher-assurance path

adversary: holder of the canonical release signing root, or anyone who coerces it
threat: canonical root used as a push-code channel into every self-hosted origin
residual_risk: an owner who pins the canonical root still trusts it, bounded by transparency and delay

adversary: Homes, PushGateways or the platform push service
threat: one platform token or Web Push endpoint handed to two parties links the profiles
residual_risk: on native a single token remains a declared linkage point unless vendor push is disabled per profile

adversary: attacker who controls the passkey provider account and obtains a copy of the browser profile
threat: one synced passkey both wraps the DeviceVault and is the RecoveryRoot, so it unseals local state
residual_risk: where only a synced passkey exists the at-rest boundary is reduced and stated

adversary: author of a theme or imported font
threat: glyph remapping makes a safety number, URL, label or prompt render differently from its string; malformed font exploits the parser
residual_risk: font sanitizers have had bugs; built-in fonts on reserved surfaces remove the spoofing channel there only

adversary: malicious plugin or mini-app in the PWA
asset: OM Core secrets and security prompts
threat: Spectre-class read of Core wasm memory from same-site code, or a mini-app drawing fake recovery/passkey prompts
residual_risk: depends on browser site isolation; plugins with content access are disabled where it is absent

adversary: T0 sponsor, or the operator/attacker of a single project-run PWA origin
threat: the origin that serves a T0 user's client code is chosen implicitly (the sponsor's, or one project origin for most users), making that party part of every such user's endpoint trust base
residual_risk: a user who explicitly opts into the sponsor's app server trusts the sponsor like their device; a compromised shared origin can still target individuals until the digest check notices

adversary: attacker controlling a template repository branch, a build-time dependency, or a stolen provisioning OAuth token
asset: code running in users' Homes and T2 ClientHosts
threat: provisioning activates code from a mutable branch outside the release trust root, or an account-wide token replaces the user's Workers
residual_risk: a compromised verifier release or release root is bounded by threshold roots and transparency, not eliminated

adversary: thief of a distribution's online advisory key, or a dominant distribution
asset: reachability between users of different distributions and profiles
threat: a malicious or compromised floor-raising SecurityAdvisory puts every relationship with other profiles or generations into 'Needs update', or forces a single-implementation profile
residual_risk: a compromised release root threshold can still sign a harmful floor until rotated; users keep override on non-threshold floors

adversary: operator of a Home running the discovery publisher, IntroGate and mailbox together (cloud vendor, T1 host or T0 sponsor)
asset: unlinkability of a user's published contact identity from mailbox activity; contact graph
threat: links the published identity to every deposit and drain, and observes contact edges among co-resident users
residual_risk: declared, not prevented: users who need separation must place the roles with different operators

adversary: sponsor who is a proximate adversary (partner, parent, employer)
asset: privacy of inbound contact and availability of the invitee's mailbox
threat: sponsor watches message timing and co-resident contacts, or revokes the mailbox to coerce or isolate the invitee
residual_risk: the sponsor sees timing for as long as the mailbox is used; the overlap window and early second route bound isolation, not observation

threat: network-level blocking of vendor IP ranges, SNI/hostnames or protocol fingerprints while the vendor keeps serving
residual_risk: a powerful censor can block every known path; OM makes no resilience claim before PR-013

adversary: state or network operator, forge or app store
threat: blocking a discovery suffix (for example workers.dev locators and invite pages), or removing the reference client from a forge or store
residual_risk: first contact through a blocked suffix fails until another locator or an out-of-band invite is used

adversary: a contact who is an estranged partner, ex-employer or stalker
threat: detects the user's presence on a shared LAN by matching relationship-derived rendezvous tags
residual_risk: a contact the user has marked can still detect co-presence by design

asset: unlinkability and contact-count privacy on a LAN
threat: counts per-contact tags to learn contact count, and links a tag set rotating together from one MAC/IP across epochs
residual_risk: platforms that do not randomize MAC addresses leave cross-epoch linkability by address

adversary: attacker of a single online release key or CI workflow; drift in the design ledger
asset: integrity of public binaries and of the proof obligations behind public claims
threat: a public binary or claim ships while its release gate is open, or a requirement is 'traced' to a conformance suite or gate that does not test it
residual_risk: the validator checks declared releases and registered suites, not whether an undeclared release is shipped
